solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Done with group of players being gloomy

parts.note: over means finished, as in 'the game is over'
the cast is the set of actors in a production

explanation.surface: A theatre company that has finished its run and feels downcast about it.
explanation.definitionFit: An overcast sky is dull and cloudy, so the weather word extends to a dark, sombre mood or look.

clue.text: Stovepipe that collapses in a heap affected with rot

indicators.note: affected here means acted upon or altered, so the letters of the words that follow are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An old top hat crushed in a pile and decaying.
explanation.walkthrough: A stovepipe is a tall top hat; the opera hat is the version built to fold flat so it could be stowed under a theatre seat.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera hat is a collapsible top hat, a gibus, which springs open and folds flat.

clue.text: English bloke holding position as well as a job

indicators.note: holding means the English bloke wraps round what follows

parts.note: gent is a colloquial word for a man
a state is a condition or position someone is in
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Englishman with both a standing in society and employment.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate agent sells and lets houses, which is an occupation, so the answer names a kind of employment.

clue.text: Tory thick Democrat cut down to size

parts.note: Con is the short form for a Conservative, a Tory in UK politics
dense means stupid as well as packed tight

explanation.surface: A dim Conservative and a Democrat put in their place.
explanation.definitionFit: Condensed text has been shortened or abridged, which is a reduction in size.

clue.text: Get cracking pastry dish south of Swiss capital

indicators.note: in a down clue the tart sits below, after the other letter
a capital letter is the first one, so the opening letter of Swiss is taken

parts.note: the word whose capital letter is taken
a tart is a pastry case with a filling

explanation.surface: An order to start baking a tart in Bern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swiss capital' looks like Bern; it means the capital letter of Swiss.
explanation.definitionFit: To start is to begin, and 'get cracking' is the idiom for beginning briskly.

clue.text: Clergyman sticks your nose in this primarily

parts.note: to pry is to meddle nosily, so this phrase gives pries

indicators.note: primarily means firstly, taking the opening letter of this

parts.note: the word whose first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A churchman who meddles in everyone's affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A priest is an ordained minister, a member of the clergy.

clue.text: One dreaded a Russian leader making a comeback

indicators.note: coming back means the letters are read in the return direction

parts.note: taken as written
the tsar was the ruler of imperial Russia

explanation.surface: A feared Russian ruler returning to power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dreaded' reads as feared, but means wearing dreadlocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Rastafarians are known for wearing dreadlocks, so one is a person with dreads.

clue.text: Shaven-headed German geezer come a cropper …

indicators.note: with the head shaved off, the first letter of the German title goes

parts.note: Herr is the German for Mr, a man; geezer is British slang for a bloke

explanation.surface: A skinhead German man takes a fall, with ellipsis leading into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To come a cropper is to make a blunder or fall badly, and to err is to make a mistake.

clue.text: … picked up visible signs of upset in rows

indicators.note: picking something up by ear means hearing it, so the clue's phrase is heard as a soundalike

parts.note: tears show that someone is upset

explanation.surface: Continuing the fallen German, onlookers notice distress in rows of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiers are layers or ranks set one above another, as in tiered seating.

clue.text: Primo coke and grass served up by young lady

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: pot and grass are both slang for cannabis
C is a slang abbreviation for cocaine
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A girl dealing top-quality cocaine and marijuana.
explanation.definitionFit: Primo is slang for first-rate, top quality, just as top-class is excellent.

clue.text: State short schoolboy tours close to Alps

indicators.note: touring around something encircles it, so the shortened schoolboy wraps the final letter
short means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: an Etonian is a pupil at Eton College, the English public school

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so the final letter of Alps

parts.note: the word whose final letter is taken

explanation.surface: A small Eton boy on a trip that ends at the Alps.
explanation.definitionFit: Estonia is a Baltic country, a sovereign state in northern Europe.

clue.text: Old black suit or watch

parts.note: to serve is to be suitable, as in 'that will serve'

explanation.surface: Choosing an old black suit or a timepiece to wear.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe is to look at closely, a synonym of the verb to watch.

clue.text: Real gold jerk stores in that case

indicators.note: storing something keeps it inside, so the gold and jerk enclose the phrase that follows

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary twitch
then means if so, in that case

explanation.surface: A genuine piece of gold is kept by some idiot, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jerk' looks like an idiot but means a twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Authentic means genuine, not fake, so it matches real in the sense of true.

clue.text: A range of men like tennis' Murray, I hear

indicators.note: a hint the clue is heard rather than spelt, giving a soundalike

parts.note: Andy Murray is the British tennis champion, so men like him are Andys

explanation.surface: A bunch of men compared to the Scottish tennis player.
explanation.definitionFit: The Andes are a mountain range running down western South America.

clue.text: One caring for canines slender aunt unleashed

indicators.note: set loose from a leash, so the letters run free into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A thin aunt lets her dogs off the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: Canines suggest dogs, which the surface plays up; here they are teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: A dental nurse assists the dentist with patients' teeth, and canines are pointed teeth.

clue.text: Get a load of a masculine idiot

parts.note: taken as written
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: Telling someone to look at a foolish macho man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get a load of' reads as 'look at', but here it literally means gather a load.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to collect or accumulate a large quantity, so to gather a load.

clue.text: A reason Slormgorm might submit to his boss?

definitions.meaning: submitting sounds like giving in, but a setter submits a puzzle for publication
the crossword editor sets the date by which work must arrive

explanation.surface: The setter wonders why he would yield to his editor.
explanation.walkthrough: Slormgorm is this puzzle's setter; 'submit' means hand in work, and the time limit for that is the reason.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadline is the latest time by which work must be handed in, the reason to deliver.

clue.text: Not at all looking forward to daughter's recital

definitions.text: Not at all looking forward to

parts.note: a reading is a performance in which a text is read aloud

explanation.surface: A parent bracing for their daughter's music recital.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreading something means anticipating it with fear, the opposite of eagerness.

clue.text: Places a colonist resettled

indicators.note: settled again in a new arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A settler is moved to new homes.
explanation.definitionFit: Locations are sites or spots, the plural noun sense of places.

clue.text: Remove first sign of degradation in cellar

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word is taken away

parts.note: abasement is humiliation, being brought low

explanation.surface: Clearing away the first trace of decay in a cellar.
explanation.definitionFit: A basement is the storey below ground level, much like a cellar.

clue.text: Rude behaviour in lake by Sweden's fantastic

indicators.note: by means next to, so the lake comes beside the rest
fantastic suggests something fanciful and transformed, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Bad manners at a Swedish lake that are amazing.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewdness is crude, indecent conduct, rude in the sense of vulgar or obscene.

clue.text: Brazilian state some pronounce a rathole

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the phrase are used, a run inside it

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Some people call a certain Brazilian state a dump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pronounce' tempts a soundalike, but the answer is simply sitting inside the words.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceará is one of Brazil's states, in the north-east of the country.

clue.text: Singers about to welcome one music producer

indicators.note: welcoming someone takes them in, so the turned-round word encloses the letter
about means turned around, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to sing is slang for informing, and an informer is a rat

explanation.surface: Vocalists greet a record producer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singers' look like vocalists; in crime slang a singer is an informer, a rat.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitar is an Indian stringed instrument, something that produces music.

clue.text: No end of excessively dull things

indicators.note: with no end, the final letter is dropped

parts.note: stuffy means stiff, boring and formal

explanation.surface: An endless supply of tedious items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No end of' reads as 'lots of', but it means cut off the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuff is a general word for unspecified items, belongings or matter.

clue.text: Song and dance in service is a gas

indicators.note: the fuss goes inside the service letters

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy, one of the armed services
a song and dance is a fuss, which is ado

explanation.surface: A naval sing-song is great fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A gas' looks like slang for great fun; here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Radon is a radioactive noble gas, a chemical element.

clue.text: Woman coming out of train unabetted

indicators.note: to train is to shape or school, so the letters are reworked into a new form

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman alights from a train on her own, with no help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming out of train' suggests leaving a carriage; 'coming out' is the debutante's entry into society.
explanation.definitionFit: A debutante is a young woman making her formal debut, or coming out, into high society.

clue.text: Members of club assisting singers

indicators.note: the members of the words are letters that belong to them, a run sitting inside

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Club members help out a choir.
explanation.definitionFit: Bassi is a plural of basso, so they are bass vocalists with the lowest voices.

clue.text: Union beginning to gel with a north African

indicators.note: the beginning of the next word is its first letter

parts.note: the word whose first letter is taken
with means together with, and
taken as written

explanation.surface: A trade union starts to bond with a man from the north of Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North African' reads as one phrase; north gives a letter and 'African' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A Ugandan is a native or citizen of Uganda, a country in East Africa.

clue.text: Whatever is a city?

parts.note: taken as written
NY is short for New York

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a given place counts as a city at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The question reads like asking which place counts as a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Any means whichever one, no matter which, as whatever does before a noun.

clue.text: Type who destroys second bottle, but not fifth

indicators.note: except the fifth letter, which is dropped from the word

parts.note: bottle is British slang for nerve or courage

explanation.surface: A vandal breaks a second bottle but leaves the fifth intact.
explanation.walkthrough: Bottle here is the British slang for nerve, not a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A scourge is a person or thing that causes great suffering or ruin, an agent of destruction.

clue.text: Female producing pork pies is very quick

parts.note: pork pies is Cockney rhyming slang for lies, so producing them is lying

explanation.surface: A woman churns out pork pies at great speed.
explanation.walkthrough: Pork pies is rhyming slang for lies.
explanation.definitionFit: Flying describes something done at great speed, as in a flying visit.

clue.text: Teacher and writer head to tavern to get wasted

parts.note: Miss is how pupils address a female teacher
a pen is something that writes

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the word whose first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A teacher and an author go to the pub to get drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wasted' suggests drunk; it is the sense of squandered.
explanation.definitionFit: Misspent describes time or money squandered, used badly, which is wasted.
